findings.issue: A git timeout is reported as EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT, whose fix hint says 'Raise timeout_seconds above N or reduce the input so extraction finishes in time.' This misleads the user. The git deadline (GIT_DEADLINE, 60 s, git.rs) is a fixed constant and the doc says it is 'not configurable'. No timeout_seconds setting exists for it, so the user cannot act on the first half of the hint. The git call may also be a rev read, a repo-root discovery or hash-object. 'Reduce the input' does not describe a hung or slow git (a stuck lock, a network filesystem, a huge repo). The Display text 'extraction timed out after 60s' also names the wrong stage.
findings.recommendation: Do not reuse the extractor timeout recovery text for git. Either (a) add a dedicated git-timeout variant or code with a hint such as 'git did not finish within 60s; check for a stalled git process, a lock file or a slow filesystem and retry', or (b) make the hint depend on the source, for example by carrying a field that says whether the deadline is configurable. If a new code is too heavy for r-7, at least change the git path to return EXTRACTION_FAILED with a detail like 'git timed out after 60s', since that code has no 'raise timeout_seconds' hint. Update the git.rs module doc and the test at git.rs:487 to match.
findings.evidence: git.rs:171, 308 and 383 call JevError::extraction_timeout(GIT_DEADLINE.as_secs()). The hint at error.rs:841-842 is unconditional. The only configurable timeout_seconds is the extractor command's (sc-jev-check/src/extract/command.rs:213).

findings.issue: The worst-case doc says 'about 17 minutes' for both LLM backends plus Jev. By the doc's own arithmetic that is 2x420 s + Jev. If Jev also gets the 90 s busy-retry budget, it is 2x420 + 210 = 1050 s, about 17.5 minutes. If it does not, the doc should say 960 s (16 minutes). The doc does not say which.
findings.recommendation: State the Jev bound explicitly, with or without busy retry, and give the total in seconds so the figure is checkable.

notes: Gates: fmt, clippy (--all-targets --all-features -D warnings, also run with --locked) and cargo test all passed on 4eb8265. HEAD matched the assigned branch and commit. The worktree was clean.

RSH-002 (git deadline, f3e25c9): closed. Every git subprocess (run, read_at_rev, hash_blob) now has a 60 s wall-clock deadline. The child is killed and reaped, the pipes are drained on their own threads, and cleanup is bounded to 2 s. Unit tests cover a hung child and a fast child. They are unix-only (cfg(all(test, unix)) with sleep and true), so the Windows path has no deadline test. This is acceptable but unproven there. A hung grandchild holding a pipe is bounded by the cleanup budget. The drain threads may outlive the call, which is harmless.

RSH-003 (judge worst-case docs, 4eb8265): closed apart from the QA-003 wording nit. The docs are in backend.rs (module and judge) and run/mod.rs, and the 420 s per-judge-call figure follows from 2 x (90 + 120) = 420. The docs state that cancel does not interrupt an in-flight request.

RSH-004 (no log on a cancelled-before-send call, f4eb939): closed. send() snapshots is_cancelled() at entry. When the token was already cancelled and the result is NetworkError::Cancelled, it returns before emit_log. Cancellation mid-send still logs. The test cancelled_before_send_emits_no_log_event covers both the cancelled case (0 events) and the live failing case (1 event). The module docs were updated.
